axioms.name: SphincsCVerify.Bridge.evm_bytecode_executes_correctly
axioms.description: EVM bytecode executes per the EVM specification (Cancun and per-chain): every external call the wallet bytecode emits on a non-reverting execute path is faithfully delivered by the EVM to its callee.
axioms.status_detail: CONTENT-BEARING since 2026-06-14 (faithfulness-audit P-FAIL fix). Upgraded from `: True` (zero-content placeholder that the falsifiability review FAILed: hostile removal broke no proof) to `∀ (c : Wallet.Execute.Call), Bridge.evmDeliversCall c`, where `evmDeliversCall : Call → Prop` is a kernel-irreducible `opaque` predicate (`the EVM transfers c.value and delivers c.data to c.target per Cancun semantics`). This is the EVM-execution boundary through which `theft_free` routes every actual value movement (the emitted-CALL byte-delivery on the execute path; the `solidityWalletExecute_compiles_correctly` doc explicitly assigns that delivery to A4, not to wallet-compilation — Halmos cannot reconstruct forwarded calldata). Present in `theft_free`'s `#print axioms` closure as a NAMED TCB MARKER via a non-consumed binding (`have _a4_delivers : evmDeliversCall (default) := evm_bytecode_executes_correctly (default)`), NOT a semantic premise — CORRECTED by faithfulness-audit pass-2 (2026-06-14): deleting that binding (axiom retained) leaves `theft_free` proven (closure drops to 9: the safety proof closes via `rw [hbridge]; exact hverify`), so `theft_free`'s genuine semantic premises are A2 (entrypoint_honest) + A3.1 (solidityVerifier) + A5 (EUF-CMA x4) + the kernel triple. The earlier 'Now LOAD-BEARING ... removing the axiom leaves it unprovable' was an OVER-CLAIM (removing the axiom DEFINITION yields an unknown-identifier error on the binding, not a logical gap). A4's content-bearing TYPE genuinely names the EVM-delivery assumption (a real honesty gain over `: True`), but A4 remains a non-consumed marker surfaced in the closure for TCB completeness; its closure presence relies on `evmDeliversCall` staying `opaque` (a `def := fun _ => True` regression would let `trivial` discharge the binding and silently drop A4 from the closure). Cited-TCB; KEVM / consensus-client conformance is the external discharge (NO in-Lean discharge artifact, NOT refactored to opaque-EQUALITY because there is no kernel-reducible Lean model of arbitrary EVM execution to equate it to — only the abstract Call-delivery predicate). Trust base is MORE HONEST, neither stronger nor weaker: 11-name `theft_free` closure (9 semantic premises + A1/A4 as named non-consumed TCB markers), A4 now NAMES the EVM-delivery assumption it always silently stood for. Never concludes `False` (conclusion is the constructorless opaque `evmDeliversCall c`), so it cannot make the system inconsistent; detonator probe still type-errors. axioms.lean_type: SM_DT_TCR_F_Shape → ITSR_F_Shape → hMsg_RO_Shape → ∀ vk transcript msg* sig*, isForgery ... → False
axioms.lean_type_note: Reduction form (2026-06-14): SM_DT_TCR_F_Shape → ITSR_F_Shape → hMsg_RO_Shape → ∀ (sk : SigningKey) transcript msg* sig*, isForgery sk transcript msg* sig* → BreaksHash, where isForgery carries KeyHistory sk transcript and BreaksHash is opaque.
axioms.status_detail: ✅ RESOLVED 2026-06-14 (was BROKEN-INCONSISTENT; see docs/EUF_CMA_INCONSISTENCY.md). Restated to a consistent reduction: conclusion is the opaque BreaksHash (never False; INVARIANT: never assume ¬BreaksHash), and isForgery is key-bound via KeyHistory sk transcript so KeyHistory sk [] forces sk to sign nothing — making the empty-transcript valid-KAT detonator UNFORMABLE. Two compiled guard lemmas (keyHistory_empty_signs_nothing, honest_sig_not_forgery; closure {propext, Quot.sound}) are the structural regression fence. Verified: the old `example : False := cannot_forge_without_breaking_SHA256 …` now fails with a type mismatch (BreaksHash ≠ False); theft_free closure is the 11 cited axioms with no sorryAx and is consistent. This is the qualitative shadow of the Barbosa et al. ASIACRYPT 2024 game (key-bound oracle log + reduction to a hardness break); the quantitative Pr ≤ ε bound is not formalised (cited, mathlib-free, out of scope). theft_free's substantive safety guarantee (conjunct 1) is EUF-CMA-FREE; this axiom only threads the cited crypto into conjunct 2. P9 (operational scope): the EUF-CMA conjunct of theft_free (conjunct 2) is NON-OPERATIONAL — `isForgery` is UNSATISFIABLE for any message the honest signer can actually sign (the project's own `honest_sig_not_forgery` lemma: a KeyHistory-bound transcript makes an honestly-produced signature never a forgery), so this conjunct threads the cited crypto hardness into the closure but does NOT bound forgeries over the operational message space; the operative safety guarantee is conjunct 1. RELATEDLY, `Spec.Signer.sign` is a placeholder spec stub (noncomputable, explicitly 'not intended to be extracted or executed', emitting all-zero FORS auth-paths + WOTS chains that do not round-trip a real verifier), so `verify_signs`'s `consistent` round-trip predicate is currently unsatisfiable for the stub — the signer-completeness (round-trip) direction rests on the Rust 10-vector KAT, NOT a kernel proof, and `verify_signs` is NOT in theft_free's dependency closure. NOT an on-chain vulnerability.

axioms.name: SphincsCVerify.Crypto.sha256_collision_resistance
axioms.description: SHA-256 collision-resistance (reduction form): equal same-length digests imply equal preimages OR a hardness break. Used by sphincsDigest_field_binding for Claim 1.
axioms.lean_type: ∀ segs1 segs2, (flatten segs1).size = (flatten segs2).size → sha256 segs1 = sha256 segs2 → flatten segs1 = flatten segs2 ∨ BreaksHash
axioms.status_detail: ✅ RESTATED 2026-06-14 (was sha256_injective_on_fixed_length, FALSE-AXIOM-LATENT). The prior literal injectivity (`… → flatten segs1 = flatten segs2`) was mathematically FALSE by pigeonhole (>32-byte inputs collide) — non-detonatable only because lean/ is mathlib-free, and it would detonate under mathlib's pigeonhole. Now stated as a consistent REDUCTION: equal same-length digests ⟹ equal preimages OR opaque BreaksHash (a distinct-same-length collision IS the cited collision-resistance break). theft_free_with_calldata_binding / sphincsDigest_field_binding now conclude the honest disjunctive form (`preimage eq ∨ BreaksHash`) and close over this consistent axiom (verified: closure = {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, sha256_collision_resistance}, no sorryAx). Cited: Barbosa et al. 2024 SM-DT-TCR (empty-ADRS unkeyed collision-resistance). See docs/EUF_CMA_INCONSISTENCY.md §4/§6.

headline_one_line: The three security claims are kernel-proven over the Lean models, and the wallet's CONTROL-FLOW surfaces are discharged on the deployed bytecode by Halmos over both compiler profiles — but the VERIFIER's full functional equivalence is NOT (the single named residual). A3.2 wallet VALIDATE: pointwise equivalence to the clause-for-clause Lean-model transcription (symbolic envelope, generic uninterpreted verifier, reachable-state invariant); the wrapper ownerIndex is covered by enumerating the entire installed set {0,1,2} + concrete reps for the unset partition + a SYMBOLIC sweep over the installed slots {1,2} (the unset partition cannot be swept symbolically — a hard Halmos dynamic-bytes-getter ceiling) + per-property rules. A3.2-exec wallet EXECUTE: pointwise equivalence of executeWithOffchainCount/executeBatchWithOffchainCount to the Lean Execute model over a SYMBOLIC (∀) ownerIndex + atomicity + credit rules. A3.3 factory: createAccount⟺precondition iff + reject rules. A3.4 owner table: add/remove/initialize pointwise vs the Lean Storage model + ownerAtIndex read parity. A3.1 verifier: discharged-bytecode on the corpus — input gates on bytecode + a FULL-functional EXECUTABLE Lean<->FIPS<->bytecode KAT (verify-test-vectors full-verify 10/10, requireFullVerify=true: accepts the 4 valid + rejects the 6 negatives) + bulk 384/384 + ~250-mutant screen; the Lean spec is now executably faithful (the chainHash/loadWord32 reconstruction bugs are fixed), with the ∀-signature symbolic equivalence the standing coverage ceiling (intractable under uninterpreted SHA-256 = A1), NOT a falsity — see docs/A3_1_VERIFIER_GAP.md. So 'fully proven to bytecode' holds for the wallet/factory/owner-table CONTROL FLOW (modulo the TCB below); the verifier's functional equivalence is carried on the corpus by the executable Lean<->bytecode KAT + bulk differential + mutant screen, not yet a ∀-symbolic proof. A1 (SHA-256) uninterpreted in every Halmos run; the uninterpreted-verifier abstraction is exactly how the wallet rules stay tractable. A2 (EntryPoint), A4 (EVM — incl. emitted-CALL byte-delivery), A5 (EUF-CMA) remain cited-TCB. Honest ceiling: a Halmos rule is a cited Halmos+z3 solver session (harness/transcription correspondences in the TCB), not a Lean proof term.
